# 03 Animate a sequence diagram's participants

## Outcome

A `sequenceDiagram` document with a `timeline:` block naming participants parses, resolves, lays
out and renders, and `render()` returns a working `AnimationController` instead of `null`.
`controller.next()` moves a participant's box, its mirror in the bottom row, and its lifeline
together — one id, every element carrying it.

## Why this ticket exists

The tracer bullet. `timeline:` in a sequence document is currently the error
`Unrecognized sequenceDiagram line: "timeline:"`, which fails the whole parse. Every stage of the
pipeline needs one carry-through change before any of it is observable, so this is one vertical
slice rather than four horizontal ones.

Participants first because they are the case ADR-0009 was written for: a preamble-declared,
never-destroyed participant is drawn three times (two rows plus lifeline) under one id, and the
controller has to reach all three. If that works, the rest is widening the valid-id set (ticket
04).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `timeline:` at the top level of a sequence document ends the diagram body and runs to end of
      file, its lines parsed by the shared `parseTimelineLine`. `SequenceDocument` gains
      `timeline: SirenTimeline | null`.
- [x] `timeline:` inside a `loop`/`alt`/`box` body is still the unrecognized-line error — a block
      body's terminator set is its own. Assert this, do not assume it.
- [x] A malformed timeline line reports the shared grammar's diagnostic (unrecognized verb, missing
      effect, effect on `unhighlight`), not a sequence-specific one.
- [x] `SequenceModel` gains `timeline: ResolvedTimeline`, resolved by ticket 01's shared
      `resolveTimeline` against a valid-id set that is **participant ids only** for this ticket.
      Naming a message or block id is the existing `references unknown id` error; ticket 04 widens
      it.
- [x] `PositionedSequenceDiagram` gains `timeline: ResolvedTimeline`, passed through
      `layoutSequence` unchanged. Assert carry-through only — the rules belong to ticket 01's seam.
- [x] `render()`'s sequence branch builds a controller with `createAnimationController` and returns
      it. A sequence document with no `timeline:` block returns a controller with `totalSteps: 0`,
      matching what a flowchart with no timeline returns — **not** `null`.
- [x] End-to-end through `render()`: `enter A fade` at step 1 leaves A's top box, bottom box and
      lifeline all carrying `siren-pending` at step 0 and all carrying `siren-enter-fade` after
      `next()`. Assert the element count, so a regression to first-match-only fails here.
- [x] `highlight` on a destroyed participant reaches its destroy mark too, which carries the
      participant's id. One id, every element.
- [x] The `render()` doc comment and `index.ts`'s dispatch comment no longer say sequence diagrams
      have no animation integration. Grep `controller: null` and the comments around
      `index.ts:108-112` and `:151-153`.

## Test seam

`parseSequenceDiagram` (through the source string) for the block; `buildSequenceModel` for
resolution; `layoutSequence` for carry-through; `render()` in `index.test.ts` for the end-to-end
claim.

- `packages/core/src/parser/parseSequenceDiagram.ts` + `.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/graph-model/buildSequenceModel.ts` + `.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/layout/layoutSequence.ts` + `.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` + `index.test.ts`

The last two were missing from the original list. Making `timeline` a required
field on `SequenceDocument` and `PositionedSequenceDiagram` forces a one-line
fixture update in each, and the worker correctly stopped rather than reaching
outside its scope. The gap was the planner's, not the worker's.

## Shared resources

None — runs alone in its round.

## Blocked by

- **02** — the ids a timeline addresses must be final before it can address them.
